items.description: A Native Recompilation Of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Nintendo Switch 2 Remake
items.readme:
Hookshot

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo Switch 2) running natively on Windows & Linux, with no emulator.

Status | How to build | In-game menu | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License

Hookshot is a static recompilation. The game's code is translated to C and compiled into a Windows program, the console's system software is reimplemented, and the Switch 2 graphics are rebuilt on Vulkan. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy. Everything the build creates (`hookshot.exe`, the generated code, the shader caches and your > saves) comes from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. ## Project status Experimental. It has only been tested on **one PC** (Ryzen 5 7600X, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB), mostly in the area at the start of the game. | What | Status | |---|---| | Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around | ✅ Works | | Sound, controller, keyboard and saves | ✅ Works | | In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling | ✅ Works | | Black flashes while moving | ✅ Fixed in testing, more play needed | | Performance without frame generation | ⚠️ About 50 fps walking, not yet a steady 60 | | Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) | ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed | | Stutter when entering new areas | ⚠️ Still happens, mostly the first time | | Ultrawide | ⚠️ The 3D keeps its shape, but the HUD is stretched and the picture is softer | | Hyrule Field and the rest of the game | ❓ Not tested yet | | AMD and Intel cards | ❓ Never tested | ## How to build The game does not come ready-made: it is built on your PC from your copy. **With Hookshot Builder, the easiest:** 1. Download the HookshotBuilder zip from the Releases page, extract it, and run `HookshotBuilder.exe`. Keep the `tools` folder beside it. 2. Choose your game's `.nup`, or your `romfs` and `exefs` folders. The builder checks that it is the right version. 3. Choose a language and a folder for the finished game, and start the build. 4. When it finishes, open `hookshot.exe` in that folder. **From the command line:** ```powershell python -I nx2/make_game.py --nup "C:\path\your-game.nup" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US ``` Or with folders: ```powershell python -I nx2/make_game.py --romfs "C:\path\romfs" --exefs "C:\path\exefs" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US ``` Add `--check` with your `.nup` or `--exefs` to only check the game's version. It builds nothing. A build takes about 40 minutes, and you can use your PC in the meantime. ### On Linux 1. Download `Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage` from the Releases page (or the Linux AppImage workflow's artifact), make it executable (`chmod +x`) and start it. It is Hookshot Builder with everything it needs inside: the compiler, the libraries and the Vulkan renderer. Nothing else has to be installed. 2. Choose your `.nup` (or your `romfs` and `exefs` folders), a language and a folder for the game, and build. 3. When it finishes, press Play. The game is also added to your applications menu, and starting the AppImage again offers Play. The game itself is `hookshot` in the folder you chose: it runs without the AppImage. From the command line: `./Hookshot--x86_64.AppImage --cli --nup ~/your-game.nup --out ~/Games/Hookshot` (the same options as `make_game.py`). You need a 64-bit x86 PC with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch, SteamOS ...), a Vulkan 1.3 driver with mesh shaders (Mesa or NVIDIA), and the same memory and disk space as on Windows. The build's own files go to `~/.cache/hookshot-builder`. Saves go in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/hookshot` (`~/.local/share/hookshot`). A `user` folder beside the game from an earlier build is moved there once. `HOOKSHOT_JOBS` sets how many files compile at once. Switches to test (`RX_VK_NOOPT=1` and the others) go in `hookshot_env.txt` beside the game, one `NAME=VALUE` a line, as on Windows. Building it yourself without the AppImage: `clang` and `lld` (LLVM 23 or newer reads the play profile; an older one builds without it), Python 3 with `lz4`, `numpy`, `capstone`, `unicorn` and `zstandard`, FFmpeg's development files (with dav1d, for the movies) and SDL2. Then `python -I nx2/make_game.py ...` as above, with `RX_CPM` pointing at a folder with Vulkan-Headers, SPIRV-Headers and VulkanMemoryAllocator in CPM's layout (`scripts/linux/deps.sh` makes one). `scripts/linux/deps.sh` and `scripts/linux/appimage.sh` make the AppImage. ### Updating to a newer release A new release is not a patch to your game folder: the game is built again from your copy, with the new code. Your saves and settings are kept. 1. Close the game. 2. To be safe, copy your saves somewhere first: the `user` folder beside `hookshot.exe` on Windows, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux. 3. Get the new release: - **Hookshot Builder:** download the new HookshotBuilder zip and extract it to a new folder (with its `tools` folder). The old builder folder can then be deleted. - **Linux:** download the new AppImage and make it executable. The old one can be deleted, the game is not removed with it. - **Command line:** `git pull` in your clone, and take the `tools` folder's contents (see [What you need](#what-you-need)) from the new HookshotBuilder zip, as they can change between releases. 4. Build again with the same `.nup` (or `romfs` and `exefs` folders) and **the same game folder** as before. With the same `.nup`, the game is not read again, but the translation and the compile still run, so it takes about as long as the first build. 5. Start the game as before. What a new build keeps and what it replaces in the game folder: | Kept | Replaced | |---|---| | Your saves (`user`, or `~/.local/share/hookshot` on Linux) | `hookshot.exe` (`hookshot` on Linux) and its files | | `hookshot_options.ini`, the in-game menu's choices | `image.bin` and the shader list | | `hookshot_env.txt` | `language.txt`, written again with the language you choose | ### What you need - The Visual Studio C++ tools and the Windows SDK. Microsoft does not allow these to be bundled, so install [Visual Studio Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) with "Desktop development with C++". The builder tells you if they are missing. - 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. - A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver. Only NVIDIA has been tested. - 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB. - About 60 GB free while building. - **Your copy of the game at the supported version:** program `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, build `e0f3ccfa`. Other versions do not work. To build from the command line you also need: - Python 3 with `lz4`, `numpy`, `capstone`, `unicorn` and `zstandard`: `pip install lz4 numpy capstone "unicorn>=2.1,<2.2" zstandard` Use Python from python.org: the Microsoft Store's Python installs packages where `python -I` does not look. - The clang from [emsdk](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk), at `C:\emsdk`. - Visual Studio 2022 with .NET 8, only if you want to change the builder itself. - The prebuilt tools that go in `third_party/`: `a64emit`, `lld-link`, `zbic` and SDL2. - What the HookshotBuilder zip carries in its `tools` folder and a clone does not. The builder sets the variables below itself; from the command line, set them before you run `make_game.py`: - `tools\cpm`: the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg. Set `RX_CPM` to this folder. Without it the build leaves out `hookshot_vk.dll`, the Vulkan renderer, and says nothing. - `tools\wgpu-native`: set `WGPU_NATIVE` to this folder. - `tools\third_party\sdl2\SDL2.dll`: copy it to `third_party\sdl2\`. - `tools\work`: copy it, with its `image` folder, to `work\`. It holds the hot-function list, the link order, the profile and the icon; without them the game builds but runs slower. ### What this does on your PC - The build reads your game and never changes it. It writes to the folder you choose and to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder`. - The romfs is hard-linked instead of copied where the disk allows it. - To uninstall, delete the game folder and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder`. ### If something goes wrong | Problem | What to do | |---|---| | "Hookshot supports build e0f3ccfa" | Check that you chose the right game with its update installed | | The game opens and closes | Update your graphics driver | | Stutter the first time you see something | Normal for now: shaders are being prepared. It gets better when you pass through the same place again | | The game is in the wrong language | Change the code in `language.txt` beside the game. The file lists them all | If the problem continues, report it with where you were in the game, your graphics card and a screenshot or video. Never send game files. ## In-game menu Press Insert in game. Everything is off by default, and your choices are saved in `hookshot_options.ini` beside the game. | Option | Choices | |---|---| | Frame generation | Off, 2x, 3x, 4x | | Frame pacing | Off, On | | Resolution | Auto (the game's own dynamic resolution), 100%, 75%, 67%, 50% | | Upscaling | Off, Catmull-Rom, Lanczos | | Sharpness | 0 to 100% | | Game speed | Per frame, Real time | | Handheld profile | Off, On | | Ultrawide | 16:9, Monitor's shape | | FPS counter | Off, On | With Game speed on Per frame, the game runs slower whenever it is below 60 fps. Real time keeps it at normal speed. ### Controls Use a controller, or the keyboard and mouse. On the keyboard, W A S D move and the arrow keys turn the camera. ## How it works 1. `nx2/lift.py` translates the game's ARM64 code to C. 2. `nx2/build.py` compiles that C together with `host/`, which plays the part of the console's system. 3. `host/nvn_native.c` records the game's NVN2 graphics calls, and `gpu/vk/` replays them on Vulkan. 4. Switch 2 Ampere shaders are lowered to Maxwell (`lower_to_maxwell.h`) and translated to SPIR-V by Eden's shader recompiler. More detail is in the [development guide](docs/development.md) and the [design notes](docs/design.md). ## Want to help? Testing on other graphics cards and reporting the result already helps a lot, and so does playing further into the game than anyone has yet. Bigger ways to help: - **Linux testing.** The Linux build (`host/posix`) has been tested on one PC so far: reports from other distributions and graphics cards help. - **Fixes in your own fork.** Fork the project, fix what you find and send the change back. Keep game files, keys and anything generated from your game out of it. ## Credits Hookshot exists thanks to the work of many people: - **NotRexed**: Hookshot, BlueShell (Mario Kart World), Skybound (Tears of the Kingdom) and the a64-kit tools. - **[Eden](https://git.eden-emu.dev/eden-emu/eden)** and **Eglantine**: the shader recompiler and Switch 2 shader work. - **suyu**: the graphics decoders and the AArch64 translator. - **[seedds/nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)**: reference for how task and mesh shaders work. - **[zortos293/Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii)**: reference for Ampere shader lowering. - **[kinnay/zbic](https://github.com/kinnay/zbic)**, **Opus** and **SDL**: decompression, audio and controllers. - **[sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp](https://github.com/sostenesfreitas/ocarina-recomp)**: this README's layout, and its notes confirmed the mesh stage's control section. - **[MythosOfs/Orchid](https://github.com/MythosOfs/Orchid)**: the fog and exposure workaround for Ocarina of Time. - **Mesa (NAK)**: the reference for Ampere's instruction encoding. - Everyone who sent fixes: klimovich008, d3zessete, chrispository, vzeol, monsterlag and leonidasmark, among others. ## License Hookshot is free software under the [GNU General Public License, version 3 or later](LICENSE) (GPL-3.0-or-later). It includes code from Eden, suyu and Orchid, which are under the GPL too. Third-party parts under other licenses that work with the GPL (Sirit, the Vulkan Memory Allocator, SDL, Opus, stb, zbic and the a64-kit tools) keep their own notices in their folders. Hookshot is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda and Ocarina of Time are trademarks of Nintendo.

items.name: quiet-md
items.description: Blazing-fast native notes app for macOS & Windows. Rust + GPUI, local-first, compatible with Feishu/Lark DocxXML.
items.readme:
Quiet.md

A fast, quiet, local notes app.
Drawn natively with Rust + GPUI. Your notes stay on your computer, stored in the Feishu (Lark) DocxXML format.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語

 

Website · Download · Performance · Features · Contributing

> [!NOTE] > Quiet.md is in **beta** and changing quickly. If you hit a bug or have an idea, please [open an issue](https://github.com/s1dashu/quiet-md/issues) — or better, send a pull request. Linux support is experimental and currently built from source; see the [Linux instructions and validation limits](CONTRIBUTING.md#linux-experimental). ## Why Quiet.md **⚡ Fast, the native kind of fast.** The whole interface is drawn on the GPU by Rust and [GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs/). No WebView, no Electron. In a one-million-character document, typing, deleting and scrolling all stay under 6 ms per frame at P95. **🔒 Local-first. Your files are yours.** No account, no cloud, and nothing goes over the network by default (the optional update check aside). Your library is an ordinary folder on your computer, and each note is one XML file. Manage it with Git, iCloud or any sync tool you like; if you ever stop using Quiet.md, your files are still there. **📝 A full rich-text editor that speaks Feishu (Lark) DocxXML.** Notes are saved in the DocxXML format used by Feishu (Lark) Docs, so copy-paste, import and export keep their structure. Headings, to-dos, tables, columns, callouts, code, math, images and attachments — the blocks you reach for when writing documents are all there. ## Download

 

| Platform | Requirements | |---|---| | **macOS** (Apple Silicon) | macOS 13 or later | | **Windows** (x64) | Windows 10 version 2004 or later | - **macOS**: unzip and drag `quiet.md.app` into Applications. The app is signed and notarized by Apple. - **Windows**: run the installer. By default it installs for the current user only, and uninstalling never deletes your notes. If SmartScreen appears on first launch, click **More info → Run anyway**. You can also download from [Quiet.md](https://quiet.md/?lang=en). Every release and its SHA-256 checksums are on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/s1dashu/quiet-md/releases). There is no Intel Mac build yet; you can [build from source](CONTRIBUTING.md#building-from-source). On first launch, Quiet.md puts a **Getting started** guide into an empty library — a ten-minute tour of the main features. Existing notes are never overwritten. The interface is available in English and Simplified Chinese. ## Performance Frame processing time over 100 consecutive operations in a mixed document of **1 million characters** and 549 chapters: | Operation | P50 | P95 | |---|---:|---:| | ⌨️ Typing | **5.06 ms** | 5.78 ms | | ⌫ Backspace | **4.99 ms** | 5.55 ms | | 🖱️ Scrolling | **2.08 ms** | 4.14 ms | A 120 Hz display gives each frame 8.3 ms. Even at P95 on a million-character document, there is headroom left. | | | |---|---| | macOS download | ~18 MB | | Windows installer | ~14 MB | | Runtime | No WebView, no Electron, no background services | Apple M5 Pro / 48 GiB, macOS 26.5, release build. Methodology and scripts to reproduce: [docs/PERFORMANCE.md](docs/PERFORMANCE.md). ## Features - **Editing**: headings, ordered and bulleted lists, to-dos, quotes, code blocks with syntax highlighting, LaTeX math, tables (with merged cells), callouts, columns, images, attachments and covers. Markdown shortcuts such as `#`, `-`, `[]` and `>`, plus a `/` slash menu. - **Organizing**: a document tree, pinning, favorites, full-text search and a trash. - **Import and export**: import Markdown and Feishu (Lark) DocxXML; export Markdown and PDF, or print directly. Pasting from Feishu or a web page keeps the structure. - **Shortcuts**: press `⌘ /` (`Ctrl+/` on Windows) to see them all. Every one can be rebound. On Windows, Ctrl stands in for ⌘ and Alt for ⌥; the app and the Getting started guides show the keys for your system. - **Themes**: four built-in styles — Craft, Feishu, Notion and Obsidian — each with a dark variant, or write your own in CSS; see [docs/THEMES.md](docs/THEMES.md). ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who has helped build Quiet.md. Issues and pull requests are welcome: building, testing and code conventions are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [![Contributors](https://contrib.rocks/image?repo=s1dashu/quiet-md)](https://github.com/s1dashu/quiet-md/graphs/contributors) ## Recent updates - **0.1.7** (Nov 6): safer multi-window saving, conflict recovery and disk writes; restricted export file access; Markdown exports keep inline attachments. Fixed Chinese input deletion with Weasel on Windows. - **0.1.6** (Nov 6): smoother window switching and typing, wider tables, regular saves during continuous typing, and Option+Space for global quick notes on macOS. Windows adds image paste, PDF export and printing, with corrected word deletion. - **0.1.5** (Nov 5): the app is now called Quiet.md; your library and notes stay where they were. - Manage several documents at once from Home: duplicate, move or delete them together. - Empty the Trash in one step; arrow keys move through the insert menu's icons; deleting every document no longer creates an empty one. - After an in-app update, the sidebar shows once what changed in the new version. - Windows: shortcuts and the built-in guide read Ctrl / Alt, and a failed launch explains itself and leaves a log. - **0.1.4** (Nov 5): - In-app updates: when a new version is out, an **Update** button appears at the top of the sidebar. The download is verified against its signature, and a restart finishes the install; open documents are saved first. Automatic checks can be turned off in **Settings › General**. A check only fetches a version manifest and sends no data. Version 0.1.3 and earlier need a one-time manual download of 0.1.4. - Dark mode: choose System, Light or Dark in **Settings › Appearance**. Built-in and custom themes all have a dark look; export and printing stay light. - **0.1.3** (Nov 4): sidebar text is readable again when macOS is in dark mode. - **0.1.2** (Nov 4): the standard macOS menus and shortcuts (Hide, Minimize, Zoom, Full Screen); clicking the Dock icon reopens a window after the last one was closed. Fixed some Chinese characters rendering with the wrong glyphs. - **0.1.1** (Nov 3): first Windows x64 release, installed per user, keeping your notes on uninstall. Polished the Chinese and English interface and the built-in guide. Full notes for each version are on [Releases](https://github.com/s1dashu/quiet-md/releases). ## License The code is licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). Third-party code, fonts and assets are listed in [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md). The following are not covered by the MIT license and should be replaced in forks: - The 67 Nucleo icons in `assets/icons/` are under a commercial Nucleo license. Do not extract or redistribute them on their own. - The name "Quiet.md" and the app icon.

items.name: player
items.description: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.
items.readme:
A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking. A few lines of code put a character in a page, a stream overlay or an app.
Comes with 21 featured characters in different styles, ready to use.

English · 中文 · 日本語 · Tiếng Việt

- WebGL2, no dependencies, about 30 KB gzipped for the core - Lip sync (microphone, audio, video) and webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), both in the browser, imported only when you need them - Plays LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters through the same API - 21 featured characters in [`characters/`](characters/), ready to use ## Try it - **Online**: the examples run on [livliv-dev.github.io/player](https://livliv-dev.github.io/player/). - **Here**: `npm install && npm run build`, serve this folder with any static server and open `/example/demo.html` (expressions, actions, microphone, camera; `?model=../characters//` picks another character). `/example/png.html` and `/example/vrm.html` show a PNGTuber and a VRM. - **On livliv.ai**: each character's page there plays it with the same renderer. Start at [livliv.ai/discover](https://livliv.ai/discover). ## Use it in your page ```sh npm install @livliv-dev/player ``` ```js import { Player } from '@livliv-dev/player' const player = new Player(document.querySelector('canvas')) await player.load('characters/k01/') // a folder with model.json and textures/, or a .livliv file player.setExpression('smile') // ids are in player.expressions player.act('nod') player.params.mouthOpen = 0.6 // 0..1 ``` Lip sync and face tracking: ```js import { createSpeech } from '@livliv-dev/player/voice' import { startFaceTracking } from '@livliv-dev/player/tracking' // needs @mediapipe/tasks-vision const speech = createSpeech(player) button.onclick = () => { speech.unlock(); speech.say('/reply.mp3') } await startFaceTracking(player) ``` A VRM or a PNGTuber, on the same API: ```js import { BodyPlayer } from '@livliv-dev/player/body' import { VrmBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/vrm' // needs three and @pixiv/three-vrm import { PngBody } from '@livliv-dev/player/png' const vrm = new BodyPlayer(canvasA, new VrmBody()) await vrm.load('/avatars/me.vrm') const png = new BodyPlayer(canvasB, new PngBody()) await png.load({ closed: 'me-closed.png', open: 'me-open.png' }) ``` The whole API is in [API.md](API.md): options, params, expressions and actions, drivers, VRM and PNGTuber characters, the limits on untrusted files, the model package and the format version. The LivLiv package format (`.livliv`, `model.json` v4) is in [FORMAT.md](FORMAT.md), with a JSON Schema in [`schema/`](schema/); packages exported before v4 are described in [FORMAT-v3.md](FORMAT-v3.md) and still play. > The npm package is the player alone. The featured characters are in this repository's [`characters/`](characters/): copy > the ones you use next to your page, with their licence. ## Featured characters `characters/` holds 21 characters, ready to `load()`. They carry a small LivLiv mark in the bottom-right corner, which the player draws. They are **not** covered by the Apache License. Most were made by LivLiv: use those free for personal, non-commercial projects with credit ("Characters: LivLiv (livliv.ai)"); don't sell them, use them commercially or train AI models on them. Nana is LivLiv's mascot. The terms are in [characters/LICENSE.md](characters/LICENSE.md). Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen come from other people's work: that licence and that credit don't cover them. Their sources, credits and terms are in [characters/CREDITS.md](characters/CREDITS.md). Each also has a `cover.webp` (512 x 768, about 50 KB), its first frame without the mark. `player.load(source, { poster })` shows it on the canvas until the first frame. To have it before any script has run, put it under the canvas with `object-fit: contain` and fade the character in over it, as [example/loading.js](example/loading.js) does. | id | name | id | name | id | name | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `k01` | Sena | `d01` | Yui | `v01` | Aster | | `k02` | Elio | `d02` | Leo | `v03` | Mira | | `char06` | Aoi | `d03` | Nana | `v04` | Kai | | `char07` | Sora | `d03ft` | Nana (refined) | `v05` | Lilith | | `s01` | Hana | `p01` | Kujira | `v06` | Usa | | `q02` | Mochi | `p02` | Kujira Q | `v07` | Stella | | `q03` | Kotaro | `p03` | Pen | `w01` | Max | ## Characters of your own You can bring in a PNGTuber's pictures, or a VRM (drawn with three.js); or make a character of your own from one picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai). - **A PNGTuber**: two pictures (mouth closed, mouth open), and two more with the eyes closed if you have them. - **A VRM**: from VRoid Studio or any tool that exports VRM 0.x or 1.0. - **A LivLiv model**: make one from a picture on [livliv.ai](https://livliv.ai), then download its model package from the character's page (**Model package**): a `.livliv` file. Pass it to `load()` as it is (a URL, or the `File` someone picked), or unzipped as a folder. Packages on the free plan carry the LivLiv mark, and the player draws it. ## About the player and the characters LivLiv Player and the `.livliv` format are LivLiv's own work. They use no Live2D software or Cubism SDK and do not read `.moc3` or `.cmo3` files. "Live2D" is a trademark of Live2D Inc.; LivLiv is not affiliated with it. Making a character on livliv.ai uses AI. The player itself only plays: it calls no AI service and reads only the files you point it at. Face tracking runs Google's MediaPipe in the browser, and camera images stay on the device; API.md has the networking details. The featured characters in this repository were made on LivLiv too, also with AI; Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen adapt other people's characters ([credits](characters/CREDITS.md)). Refined Nana (`d03ft`) also has swinging parts and head-turn keyforms added with LivLiv's own tools. A package's `meta.author` and `meta.license` record who made it and on what terms: keep them and follow them. When you show a character made with LivLiv in public, say that AI was used to make it, and don't present it as hand-drawn or hand-rigged. ## Embed without code ```html ``` The same `/live/` page has a transparent background and works as an OBS Browser Source. ## Develop ```sh git clone https://github.com/livliv-dev/player cd player npm install npm run check # types npm run build # dist/: index.js, tracking.js, voice.js, body.js, png.js, vrm.js (ES modules), chunks/ and types/ npm test # unit and fuzz tests (Node 22.18 or newer, no browser) npm run test:browser # every featured character drawn in headless Chromium; once: npx playwright-core install chromium-headless-shell npm run test:engines # a sample on Firefox and WebKit, where WebGL2 starts (a GPU or a software GL); once: npx playwright-core install firefox webkit ``` `src/runtime/` is the renderer and motion code livliv.ai runs; this repository is published from it. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Browser support WebGL2 and ES2023: Chrome / Edge 97+, Firefox 104+, Safari 15.4+. Tested on current desktop browsers, not yet on phones. ## License The code is under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE) (see also [NOTICE](NOTICE)). The featured characters have their own licence, [characters/LICENSE.md](characters/LICENSE.md). Neither licence covers the LivLiv name and logos. ## Thanks Thanks to 上善无形, ZipZipPipe and 贱兔死顺盖, whose characters Kujira, Kujira Q and Pen are based on: see [characters/CREDITS.md](characters/CREDITS.md).

# Google Pro Helper

本仓库收录两个独立版本：浏览器扩展版与批量版，分别保留各自的目录结构和原有代码。

| 版本 | 目录 | 简介 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 浏览器扩展版 | [extension](./extension/) | 在浏览器中使用的扩展项目，包含扩展清单、弹窗页面、脚本与图标。 |
| 批量版 | [batch](./batch/) | 用于批量账号任务管理的本地控制台项目，包含网页界面、后端、启动脚本与测试。 |

## 目录结构

```text
google-pro-helper/
├── extension/   # 浏览器扩展版
├── batch/       # 批量版
```
